claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has insufficient strength and plasticity for demanding fastener applications.
The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has insufficient room-temperature creep resistance.
Low-temperature aging will precipitate ordered L12 particles within the fcc lamellae of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The resulting L12 precipitates will be fine, coherent, and uniformly dispersed.
Aging at approximately 600°C for 5–10 hours is sufficient to produce the proposed precipitate distribution in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
An argon atmosphere and controlled cooling will minimize oxidation and precipitate overgrowth.
Fine L12 precipitates can strengthen an fcc phase through Orowan dislocation bowing and bypass.
The proposed aging treatment will significantly increase the yield strength of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The proposed precipitates will reduce room-temperature creep by obstructing dislocation motion.
Coherency of the L12 precipitates will limit premature crack initiation and propagation.
The aging treatment will maintain or slightly improve ductility relative to the starting alloy.
The modified microstructure may improve corrosion resistance through a more stable passivation response.
The aging treatment will maintain or slightly improve corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
The L12 precipitates will remain stable and well dispersed during thermal cycling between room temperature and approximately 700°C.
The performance enhancement will remain effective from room temperature to approximately 700°C under cyclic thermal loading.
Long-term service or thermal cycling may coarsen the L12 precipitates.
A yield-strength increase of about 20% relative to an untreated control is the proposed minimum success threshold.
